clue.text: Might well be part of a watch

parts.note: main means strength or might, as in the phrase 'with might and main'
a spring is a natural well where water rises

explanation.surface: A guess that something might well be one component of a timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might well' reads as a hedge, but each word gives a piece: MAIN (strength) and SPRING (a source of water).
explanation.definitionFit: The coiled steel strip that drives a mechanical timepiece is its main source of power.

clue.text: Some anosmia's masking unwholesome vapour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Loss of smell conveniently masks a nasty fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious, foul-smelling atmosphere once thought to spread disease.

clue.text: Not of sound mind in said French river

indicators.note: said shows the river's name is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the Seine is the river flowing through Paris

explanation.surface: Someone deranged in the river Seine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mentally unbalanced is mad, lacking reason.

clue.text: Condition of orator with nothing to say for himself

definitions.text: Condition of orator with nothing to say for himself

parts.words: Condition of orator with nothing to say for himself
parts.note: a public speaker struck dumb, the state of having no words; the word breaks into speech, less and a suffix for a state

explanation.surface: A speaker who has dried up completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being dumbstruck, unable to utter words, is the orator's plight here.

clue.text: Carefully chosen from her crèche

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters of the following words are rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: A child carefully selected out of a woman's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a light anagram signal: the answer is made from the letters of HER CRECHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché, from French, describes something rare, exquisite and sought out with care.

clue.text: Group had only the goalposts?

definitions.meaning: a football goal with no netting has nothing but its posts

explanation.surface: A team complaining their pitch had bare goalposts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer says the goal lacked netting.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical ensemble of nine players; also, split in two, the netting missing from the goal.

clue.text: Work with a hard fish

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A labourer handling a stubborn fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean species.

clue.text: Continues to exist but quietly resists change

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of resists are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that endures but softly refuses to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on lasting or endure is to carry on existing.

clue.text: Employed people should not be working on them

definitions.text: Employed people should not be working on them

parts.words: Employed people should not be working on them
parts.note: days off granted to workers, when no job is required

explanation.surface: A rule that staff ought not to work on certain days.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation days are breaks from work given to staff.

clue.text: Unusually BBC overrides us when too many shares had been applied for

definitions.text: too many shares had been applied for

indicators.note: Unusually suggests the letters of the following words come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: The broadcaster unexpectedly overrules viewers during a share offer that drew excessive demand.
explanation.definitionFit: When demand for a share issue exceeds the number available, the offer is over-applied.

clue.text: All the congregation will know this passage

definitions.text: All the congregation will know this passage

parts.words: All the congregation will know this passage
parts.note: sounds like a familiar Bible passage everyone in church can recite, but it is the walkway between pews that every worshipper walks along

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's remark that every worshipper will recognise a particular reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a text read aloud in church; it is the physical gangway down the middle of the nave.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's central gangway between the rows of pews is the passage everyone uses.

clue.text: Naval race moved from cape in Florida

indicators.note: moved tells us the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A navy's boat race relocated away from a Florida headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges NAVAL RACE into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral is the Florida headland known for rocket launches.

clue.text: Singular spectacle

parts.note: reads as 'a remarkable sight', but means one lens of a pair of glasses, spectacles cut down to the singular

explanation.surface: An extraordinary sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass for one eye is spectacles in the singular, a single lens.

clue.text: Having loitered a redhead is found in court?

indicators.note: is found in places the small pieces inside the longer word for a court hearing

parts.note: a case heard in court is tried, the question mark flagging the loose link
R is the head, or first letter, of red

explanation.surface: A loiterer with red hair turns up at the courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a red-haired person but gives just R, the first letter of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or dawdle, so the past form matches having lingered.

clue.text: Boycott land in the Midlands

parts.note: to black goods or a firm is to boycott them in trade-union usage
a country is a land or nation

explanation.surface: A call to boycott a territory in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BLACK COUNTRY is an industrial area of the English West Midlands near Birmingham; 'in the Midlands' stands for a region found there. 'Boycott' may suggest the Yorkshire cricketer Geoffrey Boycott.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Country is an old industrial district lying within England's Midlands region.

clue.text: Space allowed for removal of obstructions

definitions.meaning: the gap left so something can pass, such as headroom under a bridge
the act of clearing things away

explanation.surface: Room permitted for clearing away blockages.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom or gap left for passing; also the clearing away of things in the way.

clue.text: Inscriptions of late

parts.note: reads as 'recent writings', but means words carved for the late, the dead, on tombstones

explanation.surface: Writing that has appeared recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of late' looks like 'recently'; here 'the late' are the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Words carved on gravestones commemorate those who have died.

clue.text: Dreads the inclusion of plumage

indicators.note: inclusion of means one word is placed within another

parts.note: fears is another word for dreads, used as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone frightened at the thought of including plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's plumage is its covering of quills and down.

clue.text: Publicity hand-out on how to operate a parachute?

definitions.meaning: a statement issued to journalists by an organisation
jokingly, you push the button that frees the canopy

explanation.surface: A promotional sheet giving instructions for working a parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: An official news statement for the media; also, literally, pushing the catch that opens a parachute.

clue.text: Difficulty arising with study, it's a heavy load

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rub means a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A problem crops up with one's studies, which are a weight to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RUB upwards into BUR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty to carry, literally or figuratively, is a load.

clue.text: Cut to the point that's critical

parts.note: to sever is to cut through
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Cutting straight to the crucial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave or serious condition is one that is dangerous and acute.

clue.text: It was a big loss to shipping

definitions.text: It was a big loss to shipping

parts.words: It was a big loss to shipping
parts.note: reads like a financial setback for a shipping firm, but points to the famous liner sunk by an iceberg in 1912, whose name also means huge

explanation.surface: A remark that something cost the shipping industry dearly.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Star liner famously sank on its maiden voyage, a huge maritime disaster.

clue.text: Trainee Tom from in France entered

indicators.note: entered means one piece has gone into another

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
de is French for from

explanation.surface: A trainee named Tom arrived from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a name; it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person training for the forces or police is a recruit in training.

clue.text: Redirect battered tourer eastwards

indicators.note: battered suggests the word tourer is knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Send a dented touring car off towards the east.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something along a different path is to redirect it.

clue.text: Was not hesitant when one used the push-button switch

definitions.meaning: literally, the switch was pushed into its live position

explanation.surface: Someone acted decisively by hitting the button.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue resolutely without pause; also literally, a button pushed so a device starts.

clue.text: Denizen of the wild wood almost got a mark of rank

indicators.note: almost says the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the badger is a woodland animal, like the one in The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A woodland creature nearly earned an insignia of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Denizen of the wild wood' recalls Badger in The Wind in the Willows, who lives in the Wild Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem pinned to a uniform shows the wearer's grade or office.

clue.text: Find out about loitering with intent

definitions.meaning: to discover or work out the truth of something, informal British usage
the old British 'sus' law let police arrest people on suspicion of loitering with intent

explanation.surface: Discovering the facts of a loitering charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sus' law was a controversial British stop-and-arrest power on suspicion of loitering with criminal intent.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or discover; also the police suspicion behind a loitering-with-intent arrest.

clue.text: Be there in this

parts.note: the act of being present is what the word describes, so to be there is to be in it

explanation.surface: An instruction to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event is the very thing the word names.
